overview.mechanism: Adsorbs compounds in the gastrointestinal tract, reducing absorption of some precursors of uremic solutes.
uses: Studied as an adjunct to standard CKD care; reductions in toxin markers must be distinguished from patient-important kidney outcomes.

paragraphs.text: The randomized, placebo-controlled EPPIC-1 and EPPIC-2 trials enrolled 2,035 adults with moderate-to-severe CKD. Adding AST-120 did not significantly delay the composite of dialysis initiation, transplantation or serum creatinine doubling in either trial.

The biological rationale and changes in uremic-solute markers therefore do not establish that this treatment prevents dialysis. Trial findings should be described separately from the indication approved for the Philippine product.

sources.citation: Schulman et al. Randomized Placebo-Controlled EPPIC Trials of AST-120 in CKD. JASN. 2015;26:1732–1746. PubMed PMID: 25349205.

revision_log.change: Source-linked descriptive overview and clinical evidence; no new unsupported dose recommendation or inferred dialysis schedule.
